entries.content: I've been cooking for my family for 15 years and here's my shortcut: once you nail the timing for one protein at a certain thickness, you can apply it across the board. I do 5 minutes per side for anything cut to 2cm—chicken, pork, even turkey cutlets. The thickness is what matters most for heat penetration, and I've never had complaints at the dinner table.

Instant-read thermometers provide temperature readings in 2-5 seconds and are considered essential tools in professional kitchens. Insert the probe into the thickest part of the meat, avoiding bone contact for accurate readings.

Tested pan-frying method: 2cm cuts work great at medium-high heat, 5 min/side. Used this for chicken breast Monday, pork Tuesday, both came out juicy. The key is consistent thickness—proteins cook at similar rates when cut uniformly. No need to adjust between sessions.

The primary factors are thickness and pan temperature. For cuts around 2cm thick at medium-high heat, most home cooks find 5 minutes per side produces good results. This timing works well because heat penetration is largely governed by the distance from the surface to the center, which remains constant regardless of the protein type when thickness is matched.

Had some pork chops come out a bit pink near the bone last week even though I thought I timed it right. Ended up putting them back in the pan for another couple minutes. Kind of annoying when you think dinner is ready and it's not.
